decisions.rationale: 'enzyme deficiency' is a general term; 'deficiency' alone is excluded as too general and the phrase does not name one specific disease.
'mild or severe hemolytic anemia' joins two severity-specific disease mentions in one contiguous string, analogous to 'Stage II or stage III colorectal cancer'.
Names the single specific disease G6PD deficiency; the full string is kept as the minimum necessary span including the expanded name and abbreviation.

decisions.rationale: 'genetic abnormality' is a very general term excluded by the guidelines, not a named disease.
G6PD A is described as a nondeficient polymorphic variant, so it does not refer to a disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §1 (only annotate when the named entity clearly denotes the disease it causes)

decisions.rationale: 'enzyme deficiency' is a general term (same as candidate 1) and does not name one specific disease.
G6PD Mediterranean is a named form of G6PD deficiency explicitly associated with favism, so it is a particular disease form, like classical galactosemia.
Favism is a named, specific hemolytic disease with one definition and no further categorization.
G6PD Metaponto is explicitly described as asymptomatic, so the variant is not a disease mention in this context.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §1 (only annotate when the named entity clearly denotes the disease it causes)

decisions.rationale: G6PD Ilesha is explicitly described as asymptomatic, so it does not denote a disease in context.

decisions.rationale: G6PD Chatham is a named G6PD deficiency variant reported in a patient with neonatal jaundice, so it denotes a particular disease form.
Neonatal jaundice is a specific clinical condition with a single definition, presented as the disease manifestation in the Chatham case; it is not a general term.
Matera, identical to G6PD A-, is a named deficient G6PD variant among the mutants associated with enzyme deficiency, so it denotes a particular disease form.
Refers to the mutation of the nondeficient G6PD A variant, not to a disease.

decisions.rationale: G6PD Santiago is a named G6PD variant explicitly associated with severe chronic hemolytic anemia, so it denotes a particular disease form.
'severe chronic hemolytic anemia' describes one specific clinical condition (the Santiago presentation) rather than a family of diseases, so it is annotated as a specific disease.
